title: Importance of pore size in high-pressure hydrogen storage by porous carbons
material_description: TiC, 400, H2 ann | CDC from TiC chlorinated at 400 C (Cl2 10-15 ml/min, 3 h), H2-annealed
purification_method: annealed at 600 C for 2 h under H2 flow to remove residual chlorine (Section 2.1)
source_location: main, p. 6315 (main-2.png), Table 1, row "TiC, 400, H2 ann", column "Hydrogen uptake (77 K, 60 bar) [wt%]"
notes: area_same_sample = yes: "we would like to stress that the values included in Table 1 were measured on the same batches of CDC that were used for hydrogen storage in this work" (Section 2.2). Probe gas: Section 2.2 names Ar for surface area and porosity ("Argon sorption was conducted from relative pressure P/P0 of 10^-6 to 1 to assess porosity and surface area data"; NLDFT slit-pore PSD from Ar; SSA by BET), while Section 3 says pore characteristics were "measured under N2 and CO2 sorption"; coded Ar. BET P/P0 range not stated (10^-6 to 1 is the sorption range). Table "Pore volume" coded as total pore volume (plotted as "Total pore volume" in Fig. 3b), method not stated; average pore size from the NLDFT PSD. Porosity samples outgassed >=12 h at 300 C (for porosity analysis, not stated for H2). Lab: H2 measured with a "home-built Sieverts apparatus [21]" (ref. 21: Zhou, Wu, Hartman, Yildirim; co-author Yildirim is at NIST); the paper does not say the H2 measurement was made in another laboratory, so coded to the corresponding author (Gogotsi*, Drexel University). calibration_described = true from the Section 2.3 sentence quoted in basis_evidence (empty-volume contribution from calculated volume and known system volumes); no calibration gas or temperature stated, so free_volume_calibration is empty.
basis_evidence: "Excess adsorption isotherms were determined by measuring absolute adsorption up to 60 bar, and then subtracting the empty volume contribution using the calculated volume and known system volumes." (Section 2.3)

purification_method: annealed in NH3 at 600 C; vacuum annealing (outgassing) at 600 C (Section 3, Fig. 5)
functional_groups: surface functionalities from NH3 treatment (not identified); "the majority" removed by vacuum annealing up to 800 C
source_location: main, p. 6318 (main-5.png), Fig. 5b (Toutgas= 600 °C), series "77K", open squares (desorption)
notes: Marker centre from the white interior of the open square (hole-interior image); 42 px. Filled and open symbols = adsorption and desorption (Fig. 5 caption). isotherm_point_count left empty: at low pressure the markers of this run overlap or are hidden beneath other series, so the markers cannot be counted (log.md). PGAA (Section 3): H below 0.09%, Cl below 0.04%, Ti 0.1% before and <0.015% after vacuum annealing (unit of % not stated, so residual_metal_wt_pct left empty; the paper does not tie these to the outgassing states of Fig. 5). No surface area or pore data reported for this sample. Degassing: panel annotation "Toutgas= 600 °C"; duration and end pressure not stated. Lab: H2 measured with a "home-built Sieverts apparatus [21]" (ref. 21: Zhou, Wu, Hartman, Yildirim; co-author Yildirim is at NIST); the paper does not say the H2 measurement was made in another laboratory, so coded to the corresponding author (Gogotsi*, Drexel University). calibration_described = true from the Section 2.3 sentence quoted in basis_evidence (empty-volume contribution from calculated volume and known system volumes); no calibration gas or temperature stated, so free_volume_calibration is empty. archive: fig5b_77K_desorption.json
basis_evidence: "Excess adsorption isotherms were determined by measuring absolute adsorption up to 60 bar, and then subtracting the empty volume contribution using the calculated volume and known system volumes." (Section 2.3)
